weapon: Wand or Staff. The class doc recommends Staff: it carries more Magic ATT, and the Wand's 5% Critical Rate passive bonus does not make up the damage difference. The same page records that neither weapon's listed attack speed changes how fast Evan's skills actually cast.
secondaryWeapon: Grandis Library lists Shield and Document as Evan's secondary slots. The class doc recommends a shield in practice rather than the class-specific Document, because a shield can be Star Forced for INT, LUK and Magic ATT; it names the Deimos Sage Shield and notes its recipe drops from Normal Cygnus.
archetype: INT magician that fights as a pair with the dragon Mir. Evan casts the Circle skills (Wind, Thunder, Earth) and Mana Burst; Mir casts Dragon Flash, Dragon Dive and Dragon Breath. Casting a Circle skill while Mir is mid-skill replaces it with a fusion skill (for example Wind Circle during Dragon Flash becomes Wind Flash), and the fusion versions are where most of the damage sits. Mir's skills and the fusion skills are not affected by attack speed, which is why cooldown reduction rather than attack speed drives Evan's throughput.

linkSkill.name: Rune Persistence
linkSkill.effect: Extends the duration of Liberated Rune Power. Level 1 gives +30% Rune duration; level 3 gives +70% Rune duration and +5% Damage.
linkSkill.note: MapleDoro states the level-3 value as +70% Rune duration and does not mention the damage line; MapleStory Wiki's skill table carries both the +70% duration and the +5% Damage at level 3. Two independent sources, no contradiction, the wiki is the fuller reading.

legionEffect.effect: Chance on attack to recover a percentage of Max MP, with a 10 second internal cooldown. Recovery scales +2% / +4% / +6% / +8% / +10% across Legion ranks, at a 70% trigger chance.
legionEffect.consensus: moderate - two sources outside each other's lineage state the same numbers.

priority.why: The class doc's Skill Nodes page puts it at the top of the High Priority list with the words MUST MAX FIRST FOR BOSSING, states that the higher the skill level the longer its duration, and says to always place it into a Lv. 5 Enhanced Node slot when bossing.
priority.verbatimAnchor: MUST MAX FIRST FOR BOSSING.  The higher the skill level, the longer its duration.  Always place into a Lv.5 Enhanced Node Slot when bossing.
priority.consensusNote: Class doc only. Grandis Library publishes no V skill node ranking for Evan, and no source outside the Evan Discord lineage ranks Evan skill nodes. This is the one skill node the doc explicitly ranks first, so the ordinal is the doc's own, not an inference.

priority.why: Listed second in the class doc's High Priority group, described as a high efficiency skill for EXP and Item Drop Rates, with the instruction to always place it into a Lv. 5 Enhanced Node slot when training (i.e. the training counterpart to Elemental Radiance's bossing slot).
Evan's bind. The class doc gives a concrete floor: enhance to at least Lv. 25, with or without an Enhanced Node slot.
priority.consensusNote: Class doc only. The Lv. 25 floor is stated verbatim; no reason for the number is given on the page.
priority.correctionNote: An earlier version of this file attached the rationale "so its cooldown lines up with Elemental Radiance's". That rationale appears nowhere on the cited page and has been deleted.

priority.node: Spiral of Mana, Dragon Slam, Elemental Barrage, Maple Goddess Blessing, Mana Overload (V skill nodes)
priority.why: The remainder of the class doc's High Priority group, listed in that page order after the three above. Spiral of Mana is a plant-down skill with 100% uptime that also grants passive Magic ATT and needs an input command (Mana Burst + Down Arrow + Mana Burst). Dragon Slam levels up alongside Wyrmking's Breath and Ludicrous Speed. Elemental Barrage grants a stackable 5% Final Damage buff, up to 4 stacks, for 10 seconds, and is used with Dragon Slam to cast Wyrmking's Breath - the doc warns the buff will not activate if used with Dragon Slam while crouched. Maple Goddess Blessing requires Maple Warrior or equivalent to be active before casting, has a 180 second charge cooldown and holds up to 2 charges. Mana Overload is a toggle that trades MP per cast for Final Damage.
priority.orderedNote: The class doc prints these five in a fixed page sequence but states no ranking among them, so no order is asserted here. Only Elemental Radiance carries an explicit ordinal on that page.

priority.why: The class doc's Medium Priority heading, below the High Priority group and with no internal ranking: Freud's Wisdom, Erda Shower / Erda Fountain, Decent Speed Infusion, Decent Sharp Eyes, Blink, Rope Lift, Ethereal Form, Will of Erda, Decent Combat Orders, Decent Holy Fountain.

priority.why: The class doc's third and lowest heading. Decent Advanced Blessing is listed as low priority; Decent Mystic Door and Decent Hyper Body are both labelled ZERO USE. All three are kept in the matrix only for their scaling passive all-stat lines.

Trio 3 - Magic Debris + Dragon Dive + Dragon Spark

boostNodeTiers.howVerified: Grandis renders the tier as a colour, not as text, which is why three separate text-extraction reads of this page produced three different and mutually contradictory splits. Resolved from the page's own machine-readable state instead: the embedded page data carries "primary":[0,1,2,3,4,5] for Evan and no "secondary" key, and all six rendered node blocks carry the identical colour token #2E94B6. vMatrix.notes: The two framings that an earlier pass recorded as an unresolved conflict are not in conflict. Grandis Library publishes BOTH a six-group node listing and a three-trio recommendation, and its trios match the class doc's and mastermysty's trios in membership and in across-trio order. Magic Debris and Dragon Spark are not demoted by Grandis: they sit in its Tertiary Trio, and its node-group tiering marks every Evan group Primary, so it demotes nothing. On Enhanced Node slots, the only sourced guidance remains the Lv. 5 slot going to Elemental Radiance for bossing and to Decent Holy Symbol for training; the class doc's Special Nodes page covers only the shared boss nodes and the temporary nodes and gives no Evan-specific enhancement ranking.

hexa.orderStatus: NOT SOURCED. Re-checked in full on 2026-09-12; no public source reachable in this pass publishes an Evan HEXA investment order in readable text. Four dead ends: (1) the class doc's HEXA Matrix Resources page (https://sites.google.com/view/evanandmir/navigate/6thjob/resources) contains no order at all - only a link to a personal progression spreadsheet plus the line 'For general HEXA progression guide, see Infographics'; (2) that spreadsheet ('Evan 6th FD Progression (P) v7 Ascents') is not publicly exportable - a CSV export request returns HTTP 400; (3) the class doc's general HEXA progression guidance exists only inside an infographic image; (4) Grandis Library's Evan page has no HEXA section whatsoever, only a '6th Job' infographic image credited to the Evan Discord. MapleDoro's Evan 6th job section is explicitly marked 'Work in Progress' and tells readers to consult the class document or class Discord. An order is deliberately left empty rather than guessed.

origin.breakpoints: Lv. 10 - Ignore Defense: +20%. Lv. 20 - Boss Damage: +20%. Lv. 30 - Ignore Defense: +30%, Boss Damage: +30%.
origin.detail: Master Level 30, active. Cooldown 360 seconds, duration 45 seconds, invincible during casting. Targets the boss with the highest Max HP first and is unaffected by attack reflection.
origin.consensusNote: Skill data rather than judgement. Breakpoints read verbatim off the class doc; names cross-checked against the wiki skill table.

ascent.breakpoints: Lv. 10 - Ignore Defense: +10%, Boss Damage +10%. Lv. 20 - Ignore Defense: +10%, Boss Damage: +10%. Lv. 30 - Ignore Defense: +20%.
ascent.skillEffect: The skill itself applies Ignore Defense +60%, Boss Damage +40% and Critical Rate +100% during its attack.
ascent.cooldownNote: The class doc lists Cooldown: 240 seconds and then states that Ascent skills can be used up to THREE (3) times in a boss fight with no cooldown. It adds that Ascent skills can only be used while a boss with the highest max HP is present, do not trigger additional attacks or combat effects, and ignore stat contributions from hat, ring, conditional passives, active skill effects, link skills, enemy attributes and patterns, and items under 30 minutes duration.
ascent.correctionNote: An earlier version said 'The wiki's skill table lists no cooldown on it.' The class doc does list a 240 second cooldown alongside the three-free-casts rule; the two are not in tension and the bare claim has been replaced with what the page actually says.

masteryCores.structure: Four Mastery cores, and the grouping is unusual - one core upgrades several skills at once.
masteryCores.prerequisites: Each HEXA Mastery skill requires its base skill at a stated level - HEXA Mana Burst requires Mana Burst IV Lv. 30+, HEXA Thunder Circle requires Thunder Circle Lv. 10+, HEXA Dragon Flash requires Dragon Flash. The fusion Mastery skills (HEXA Thunder Flash, HEXA Wind Flash, HEXA Earth Dive, and so on) instead require their parent Mir skill at Lv. 30 Boost Node Enhancement.
masteryCores.inheritanceNote: Both sources state that Mastery skills are affected by Hyper Skill passives (where applicable) and by Boost Node enhancements applied to the base skill. That is the mechanical link between the V matrix boost nodes above and 6th job output, and it is why a boost node on a base skill keeps paying after 260.
masteryCores.consensusNote: Only MapleStory Wiki states the grouping, and it states it explicitly: its Mastery Skills table is headed 'Mastery Node/Core 1' through 'Mastery Node/Core 4' with exactly this membership. This is a structured data table rather than an opinion, which is why it is recorded despite a single source. The class doc's HEXA Skills page lists the same fifteen HEXA Mastery skills in exactly this sequence but applies no group headings of any kind - every skill name on that page carries identical styling and there are no dividers - so it corroborates the ordering but does not independently state the four-core grouping.
masteryCores.correctionNote: An earlier version of this file rated this 'strong on the facts' on the stated basis that the class doc lists the same four groups. It does not; it lists no groups. That corroboration was fabricated and the rating has been dropped to weak. The adversarial pass's counter-claim - that the class doc lists FIVE groups organised by skill family, with the three Circles kept together - is also not on the page: the page's actual sequence is Mana Burst, Thunder Circle, Dragon Flash, Thunder Flash, Wind Flash, Earth Circle, Dragon Dive, Earth Dive, Thunder Dive, Wind Circle, Dragon Breath, Earth Breath, Wind Breath, Magic Debris, Dragon Spark, which splits the Circles apart and matches the wiki's four cores exactly. The four-core structure is correct; only its stated basis was wrong.

The class doc prints the curve: +11% at Lv. 1, +25% at Lv. 10, +40% at Lv. 20, +49% at Lv. 29, +60% at Lv. 30 - linear between the jumps at 10, 20 and 30. Elemental Barrage Boost additionally cuts Elemental Barrage's cooldown by 5 seconds at Lv. 6, 11, 16, 21 and 26, from 55 seconds at Lv. 1 down to 30 seconds from Lv. 26 onward.

hexaStat.rule: Any attribute (for example Magic ATT) can be used TWICE as a Main Stat and TWICE as a Sub Stat across all six Stat Nodes.

hexa.notes: The practical finding for this class stands after re-checking: Evan's HEXA investment order is not a list anyone has published in text. hyperStats.priorityStatus: NOT SOURCED. Re-checked in full on 2026-09-12 against every source in this file. The class doc's General Stats page has no hyper stat section - it covers Will of the Alliance, Inherited Will, inner ability, critical rate, attack speed, hyper passives, legion artifact and link slots, and the only appearance of the words 'Hyper Stat' anywhere on it is in the line 'Supplement the remainder with: Hyper Stat | Legion Grid | Lynn Link Skill' under critical rate. Mesos Obtained or Item Drop Rate +15%

doNotRoll.claim: Attack Speed +1 is no longer needed on Evan inner ability.
doNotRoll.why: The class doc states verbatim 'GMS v.267: Evan will no longer require AS(10) from Inner Ability' and lists the sources that reach the cap without it: base +4, Magic Booster passive +2, Decent Speed Infusion +1, Monster Park Green Potion +1 (marked as breaking the cap), Return! - Dive +1.
doNotRoll.consensusNote: The judgement is the class doc's alone; the mechanical components are confirmed against the wiki's skill table.

gearingNotes:
Several things change for Evan specifically.

WEAPON. Staff over wand. The class doc's reasoning is that the staff's higher Magic ATT beats the wand's 5% Critical Rate passive. It also records that the attack speed printed on either weapon does not change how fast Evan's skills cast, so picking a weapon for its speed rating is wasted. Grandis Library's derived base stats agree that a wand adds 5 points of crit rate (+50% from passives without one, +55% with).

SECONDARY. Evan has a class-specific Document secondary, but the class doc recommends a shield instead - it names the Deimos Sage Shield, whose recipe drops from Normal Cygnus - because a shield can be Star Forced for INT, LUK and Magic ATT.

WSE POTENTIAL TARGET. The class doc's general recommendation is 9 lines of Magic ATT, or 8 lines of Magic ATT plus 1 line of Boss Damage, while pointing out that the right answer depends on familiars, buffs, guild skills and HEXA stat and should be checked against a damage calculator.

DRAGON GEAR. Mir has four equipment slots of his own - mask, pendant, wing and tail - which no other class has. The class doc's progression: the Silver set comes from the Evan story questline (2 INT and 2 LUK in total), the Gold set is bought from Neville the secondary equipment vendor (4 INT and 4 LUK), the Reverse set is crafted through Smithing without a recipe (6 INT and 6 LUK), and the Abyss set is crafted from recipes sold by the Celestial Robes and Abyss vendors (10 INT, 10 LUK and 1 Magic ATT), limited to one craft per recipe. Reverse and Abyss pieces can each be levelled three times, gaining 0 to 1 INT and 0 to 1 LUK per level.

COOLDOWN HAT. This is the biggest Evan-specific gearing decision. Because Mir's skills and the fusion skills ignore attack speed entirely, cooldown reduction is what raises Evan's damage. The class doc names -2 seconds with 20% INT as the Heroic target, with -2 seconds and 23% INT or -4 seconds and 10% INT as the double-prime rolls worth keeping, and -5 seconds for Interactive worlds where bonus potential is available. It lists what the reduction touches: the four Mir skills (Dragon Flash, Dragon Dive, Dragon Breath, Dragon Slam), the fusion skills attached to them, Freud's Wisdom, HEXA Elemental Barrage, Wyrmking's Breath, Blink and Ethereal Form. The doc also says the hat became noticeably more valuable after recent patches. Separately, a hat of at least -5 seconds combined with an SSS Mercedes card is the gate on the alternative hyper passive loadout recorded above.

CRITICAL RATE. Evan arrives at roughly 90% crit from its own kit plus normal account progress, per the class doc's breakdown. Dark Fog adds a further 20% crit rate while active, but it is a 40 second cooldown buff rather than a permanent line, so it should not be counted toward the standing total.

LINK SLOTS. For bossing the class doc ranks the twelfth slot as Noble Fire (Adele) in parties of three or more, then Tree of Stars (Sia Astelle), Focus Spirit (Lynn) where crit rate is short, Spirit of Freedom (Resistance) for survival, and Innate Gift (Khali). For training it suggests Combo Kill Blessing (Aran), swapped for Phantom Instinct (Phantom) if crit rate is short, and Tides of Battle (Illium) on maps that require movement.

LEGION ARTIFACT. The class doc's bossing order is Damage 15%, Boss Damage 15%, Ignore Enemy Defense 20%, Critical Damage 4%, All Stats 150, Magic ATT 30, Cooldown Skip 7.5%, Final Attack skill damage 30%, Buff Duration 20%, Summoned Minion Duration 20%, with Critical Rate 20% called out as the broadest account-wide benefit. Training uses mesos, drop rate and experience at 12% each.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rolling for +1 attack speed on inner ability.
commonMistakes.why: The class doc states Evan no longer needs it as of v.267 - the cap is reachable from Agile Magic, Magic Booster, Decent Speed Infusion, a Monster Park potion and the Return Dive fusion. A Return Dive cast also buffs nearby party members' attack speed.

commonMistakes.mistake: Choosing a weapon by its attack speed rating.
commonMistakes.why: The class doc records that the attack speed on either Evan weapon does not change actual cast speed, so the choice is purely a stat comparison.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting a HEXA Mastery core to be usable before the base skill is capped.
commonMistakes.why: Each HEXA Mastery skill carries a required level on its base skill - Mana Burst IV at 30 for HEXA Mana Burst, Dragon Flash at 20 for HEXA Dragon Flash, Thunder Circle at 10 for HEXA Thunder Circle, and so on. The class doc makes the same point in general terms.

commonMistakes.mistake: Treating cooldown reduction as a minor stat on Evan.
commonMistakes.why: Mir's skills and the fusion skills are explicitly unaffected by attack speed increases, per the wiki's own skill descriptions, so cooldown is the lever that controls how often they fire. The class doc builds its hat targets around exactly this.

skillBuildPath.note: Grandis Library presents this as an example order, notes that every 1st through 4th job skill can eventually be maxed, and advises putting one SP into each skill before maxing anything.
skillBuildPath.consensus: weak - Grandis Library only. Its skill build path is not one of the three fields it credits to the class doc, so provenance for this section is unstated.

earlyGameNotes.hyperPassiveTiming: The three Speedy passives unlock at Lv. 140; Howling Wind at 150 and Lungs of Stone at 165; Rolling Thunder and Earth-Shattering Dive at 180; Cyclone Breath at 190. A Lv. 128 character has none of them yet.

sources.what: Evan and Mir - the Evan class doc, written by Evanovation (GMS Heroic, Kronos), presented as a compilation of the MapleStory Evans Discord. Pages re-read on 2026-09-12 for this pass: General Stats (/navigate/stats), 5th Job TriNodes and Skill Nodes, 6th Job HEXA Skills (/navigate/6thjob/skills), HEXA Matrix Resources (/navigate/6thjob/resources - note: NOT /hexamatrixresources, which 404s) and HEXA Stat (/navigate/6thjob/hexa-stat). This is the primary and in most endgame fields the only judgement source for Evan.
sources.dated: Every page footer reads 'Site last updated: November 12, 2025', GMS Patch v.264, KMS Patch v.1.2.407. CAVEAT: the footer understates the content - the HEXA Skills page describes HEXA Freud's Wisdom as 'coming soon to GMS v.271', so the doc is maintained past its own date stamp.

sources.what: Grandis Library's Evan page. Carries six numbered boost node groups with a Primary/Secondary/Other legend (all six tagged Primary for Evan, so the legend discriminates nothing here), a separate Primary/Secondary/Tertiary TRIO recommendation matching the class doc's Set A/B/C, the hyper skill passive build, recommended inner ability for bossing and training, an example skill build path, base stats derived from Evan's own passives, class properties and the legion effect. No HEXA section exists on this page - only a '6th Job' infographic image credited to the Evan Discord, dated 2026-06-25.
sources.dated: Sitewide stamp GMS Ver. 269 (Ride the Lightning Update) - two patches behind v.271.

Read it from the page's embedded machine-readable state instead ("primary":[i,...] and optional "secondary":[i,...], with unlisted indices meaning Other), calibrating colours against a sibling class page whose split is non-trivial.

sources.what: MapleStory Wiki's full Evan skill table. Used as the name-validation and mechanics authority: exact skill names for every job, the nine hyper passives and three hyper actives with level requirements (140/150/165/180/190 and 140/160/190), the Rune Persistence link skill, HEXA Origin (Zodiac Burst) and Ascent (United Horizons), the four Mastery Node/Cores with their membership and prerequisites, the four HEXA Enhancements, and the Sol Hecate common core. Carries no priority judgement of any kind.
sources.dated: Living wiki page; revision history could not be reached, so the date is unverified. Content includes Sol Hecate: Phlegethon and Pactum, so it is current to the 6th job era.

sources.what: The MapleStory Evans Discord, linked from both Grandis Library and the class doc. Upstream of everything above. Not machine-readable here.

consensusExplanation: Four independent sources were reached; two carry judgement and only one of those covers more than boost node trios. By field: the across-trio boost node priority is the strongest judgement claim in the file, stated in the same sequence by the Evanovation lineage and independently by mastermysty - moderate. Trio membership is likewise moderate; trio-internal sequence is not a claim at all and is stored unordered. Hyper passive loadouts are one judgement lineage with every name and effect wiki-verified - moderate on the facts, weak on the loadout choice. HEXA skill names, breakpoints, prerequisites and Enhancement effects are data rather than opinion and are confirmed across the class doc and the wiki - moderate. The HEXA Mastery core grouping rests on the wiki alone - weak, despite being structural data. V skill node priority, boost node tiering, HEXA stat, inner ability and the alternate hyper passive build all rest on the class doc alone - weak. Hyper stat priority and HEXA investment order have no source at all and are left empty. Overall: weak.

conflicts.topic: Internal sequence within the boost node trios
conflicts.status: RESOLVED - there is no ordering claim to be in conflict about.
conflicts.finding: All three sources print the same three members for each trio in three different sequences, and two of those three sources are the same author. Trio 1: class doc Wind/Thunder/Earth, Grandis Wind/Earth/Thunder, mastermysty Wind/Earth/Thunder. Trio 2: class doc Mana Burst/Dragon Flash/Dragon Breath, Grandis and mastermysty Mana Burst/Dragon Breath/Dragon Flash. Trio 3: class doc Dragon Dive/Magic Debris/Dragon Spark, Grandis Dragon Spark/Dragon Dive/Magic Debris, mastermysty Magic Debris/Dragon Dive/Dragon Spark.
conflicts.resolution: Since Evanovation publishes two different sequences for the same trios in two places, sequence within a trio cannot be a recommendation. Trios are now stored as unordered sets with ordered:false and the published sequences recorded verbatim for reference. The across-trio priority, on which all three sources do agree, is stored separately.

conflicts.topic: Where Magic Debris and Dragon Spark belong
conflicts.status: RESOLVED - the conflict was an artefact of a bad read of Grandis.
conflicts.finding: Grandis Library does not demote Magic Debris or Dragon Spark. They appear in its Tertiary Trio alongside Dragon Dive, and in its node-group listing they sit in Node 6 which - like all five other Evan node groups - is tagged Primary. mastermysty's not-needed note names only Dragon Master, Summon Onyx Dragon and Dark Fog, never Magic Debris or Dragon Spark. The sources agree.

conflicts.topic: Dragon Master's value as a boost node
conflicts.positionA: Grandis Library includes Dragon Master in node group 5 and tags that group Primary - though it tags all six Evan groups Primary, so the tag does not single Dragon Master out.
conflicts.positionB: mastermysty heads a row 'Not needed in the 6th job Mastery' containing Dragon Master, Summon Onyx Dragon and Dark Fog.
conflicts.status: contested, narrowed. The narrow factual point is settled: Dragon Master appears in none of the four HEXA Mastery cores on the wiki, and in none of the wiki's HEXA Enhancement boost lists. Grandis's own legend defines Primary as nodes that unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery, which Dragon Master does not - so its tag is inconsistent with its own legend here. What is still unsettled is whether a Dragon Master boost node is worth building before 260, which no source states either way.
conflicts.note: mastermysty's page is dated 2024-11-21. Not resolved here.

conflicts.finding: MapleStory Wiki states the grouping explicitly under headings 'Mastery Node/Core 1' to 'Mastery Node/Core 4' with the membership now recorded in hexa.masteryCores. The class doc's HEXA Skills page lists the same fifteen HEXA skills in exactly that sequence but applies no headings, dividers or differentiated styling, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the grouping - it simply does not state one. The earlier 'strong' rating cited the class doc as corroboration it does not provide; the rating is now weak and the source list is the wiki alone.

conflicts.positionA: Grandis Library lists Evan's secondary slots as Shield and Document.
conflicts.positionB: The class doc recommends a shield specifically and says not the class-specific Document, because a shield takes Star Force for INT, LUK and Magic ATT.
conflicts.status: not a real conflict - Grandis is stating what Evan can equip, the class doc is stating what to equip. Recorded so the two are not mistaken for disagreement.

conflicts.positionA: The site footer on every page reads "Site last updated: November 12, 2025", GMS Patch v.264 and KMS Patch v.1.2.407.
conflicts.positionB: The doc's own HEXA Skills page describes HEXA Freud's Wisdom as 'coming soon to GMS v.271', and its Infographics page carries a general infographic stamped GMS v.271, so it is being maintained past its own footer date.
conflicts.status: internally inconsistent but in the useful direction. The doc is current enough to reference v.271 content. Grandis Library is separately stamped v.269 sitewide, though its Evan infographics are dated 2026-05-25 and 2026-06-25.

gaps: No hyper stat priority exists for Evan in any reachable source. Re-confirmed 2026-09-12 against the class doc, Grandis Library and MapleDoro.

No HEXA investment order exists in readable text anywhere public. It lives in an infographic image and in a per-character spreadsheet that is not publicly exportable. This is the single largest hole in the file.
No source ranks the four HEXA Enhancement cores against each other.
The class doc covers only the first three of the six HEXA Stat nodes.

Only two independent judgement lanes exist for this class - the Evanovation lineage (class doc, restated by Grandis Library) and mastermysty, whose page is dated 2024-11-21 and covers boost node trios only. The Evan Discord is not machine-readable and reddit is blocked in this environment.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm.
clearedOnInspection: NO invented skill or node names found. This is the file's strongest result and it should be said plainly. I verified verbatim against the cited pages: all eight high-priority and ten medium-priority V skill node names; all nine trio skills in both sources; all six Grandis boost node group memberships; HEXA Origin 'Zodiac Burst' and Ascent 'United Horizons'; all four Enhancement cores (Elemental Barrage Boost, Dragon Slam Boost, Elemental Radiance Boost, Spiral of Mana Boost); the Common cores including Sol Hecate and its Styx/Charon/Phlegethon/Pactum sub-skills; all three HEXA stat nodes with main/additional stats and level gates; every hyper passive including the alternate build; the inner ability lines; the Deimos Sage Shield and its Normal Cygnus recipe; and the spreadsheet title 'Evan 6th FD Progression (P) v7 Ascents'. Every one matched.
contest.resolutionMethod: Each disputed endgame claim was re-checked by fetching the exact cited page and reading the relevant section verbatim. Grandis Library's boost node tiering, which is rendered as colour rather than text and had produced three mutually contradictory text-extraction reads, was resolved from the page's embedded machine-readable state and calibrated against sibling class pages where the tier split is known to differ.

resolved.defect: MISREPORTED, and it is the claim labelled 'strong': the HEXA Mastery core grouping does not match the class doc it cites.
resolved.outcome: PARTLY CONFIRMED - claim kept, basis corrected, rating dropped.
resolved.whatIDid: Read both pages. The critic is right that the class doc does not corroborate a four-group structure, and the 'strong' rating was built on corroboration that does not exist. The critic's own counter-reading is also wrong: the class doc's HEXA Skills page is a flat, ungrouped list of fifteen HEXA Mastery skills in the sequence Mana Burst, Thunder Circle, Dragon Flash, Thunder Flash, Wind Flash, Earth Circle, Dragon Dive, Earth Dive, Thunder Dive, Wind Circle, Dragon Breath, Earth Breath, Wind Breath, Magic Debris, Dragon Spark - every name identically styled, no headings, no dividers. It does not keep the Circles together and it does not list five family groups. MapleStory Wiki, which the earlier pass could not reach and which I reached this pass, states the grouping explicitly under headings 'Mastery Node/Core 1' through 'Mastery Node/Core 4' with exactly the membership the file already had. So the four-core structure is correct and is retained, sourced now to the wiki alone: sourceCount 1, consensus weak, with a note recording that the class doc's sequence is consistent with it but asserts no grouping. The downstream conclusion about Dragon Master survives, as the critic expected.

resolved.defect: LIKELY MISREPORTED: the Grandis boost node tier assignment (file: secondary = Groups 2, 3, 4; other = Group 6).
resolved.outcome: CONFIRMED as a defect - old split DELETED, replaced with the verified state.
resolved.whatIDid: Neither the file's split nor the critic's was on the page. Grandis renders the tier as a colour, not as text, which is why the file's pass, the adversarial pass and a fresh text extraction each produced a different answer. Resolved from the page's own embedded state instead: the Evan page data carries "primary":[0,1,2,3,4,5] and no "secondary" key, and all six rendered node blocks carry the identical colour token #2E94B6. Calibrated against sibling class pages where the split is real - Aran carries "primary":[0,1,2,3],"secondary":[4,5] and renders four #2E94B6 blocks then two #CC6A2A blocks; Hero and Kaiser match the same pattern. Conclusion: ALL SIX Evan node groups are tagged Primary; Evan has no Secondary and no Other tier, so the tiering carries no discriminating information for this class. The old primary/secondary/other split is deleted. Group memberships, which were correct, are retained and re-verified verbatim. A separate find: Grandis also publishes a Primary/Secondary/Tertiary TRIO recommendation for Evan that the file had never recorded, and it matches the class doc's and mastermysty's trios - that is now in vMatrix.trios.

resolved.defect: UNRECORDED CONFLICT: the file logs differing internal trio sequence for trios 2 and 3 but not for trio 1, which differs too.
resolved.outcome: CONFIRMED - and fixed at the structural level rather than by logging a third conflict.
resolved.whatIDid: Verified verbatim: the class doc's TriNodes page reads 'Set A: Wind Circle, Thunder Circle, Earth Circle' while mastermysty reads 'Trio #1: Wind Circle, Earth Circle, Thunder Circle'. The critic is right that all three trios disagree on sequence, not two. Grandis adds a third data point and makes the finding decisive: its Primary Trio reads Wind, Earth, Thunder - a different sequence from the class doc for the same trio by the same credited author. Since one author publishes two different sequences for the same trio, sequence cannot be carrying a recommendation. Rather than log a third unresolved conflict, the data structure was changed to stop asserting one: trios are now unordered sets with ordered:false, each source's published sequence recorded verbatim under sequencesAsPublished, and the across-trio priority - on which all three sources DO agree - stored separately as an explicit ordered claim at moderate consensus.

resolved.defect: Unsourced rationale on Erda Nova: 'at least level 25, so its cooldown lines up with Elemental Radiance's'.
resolved.scope: in scope (vMatrix) - found during resolution, not in the original defect list
resolved.whatIDid: The cited Skill Nodes page says only 'Erda Nova: (Bind Skill) Enhance to at least Lv.25 (with or without Enhanced Node Slot)'. It gives no reason, and says nothing about lining up with Elemental Radiance's cooldown. The Lv. 25 floor is kept; the invented rationale is deleted.

resolved.defect: Unsourced claim on the Ascent skill: 'The wiki's skill table lists no cooldown on it.'
resolved.whatIDid: The class doc does list Cooldown: 240 seconds for United Horizons, immediately above the note that Ascent skills can be used up to three times per boss fight with no cooldown. The bare assertion about the wiki was replaced with what the class doc actually prints.

resolved.defect: Gap: 'the wiki's HEXA Enhancements table was not read, so the four Enhancement core names rest on one source.'
resolved.scope: in scope (hexa) - carried gap rather than a defect
resolved.whatIDid: Reached the wiki's HEXA Enhancements section this pass. It lists Elemental Barrage Boost, Dragon Slam Boost, Elemental Radiance Boost and Spiral of Mana Boost - all four names confirmed, matching the class doc. The Enhancement cores move from weak/1 source to moderate/2 sources. The class doc's numbers were also read verbatim and confirm +60% Final Damage at Lv. 30 on each, and Elemental Barrage's cooldown dropping to 30 seconds from Lv. 26.

stillOpen: Dragon Master's value as a boost node before Lv. 260 remains contested between Grandis (includes it in a node group) and mastermysty (not needed in the 6th job Mastery). The narrow factual point - that Dragon Master is in none of the four HEXA Mastery cores - is settled in mastermysty's favour by the wiki. Whether the node is worth building pre-260 is stated by no source and is recorded in conflicts rather than decided.
contest.shipReadyNote: Every claim in vMatrix, hexa, hyperSkills, hyperStats and innerAbility has been re-verified against a re-fetched cited page in this pass and carries sources, sourceCount, consensus and verifiedAt. Two sections are deliberately empty rather than guessed: hexa.order and hyperStats.priority. An empty, labelled gap is not an unverified claim.
